identity.resolvedIdentity: The preserved main and administration building of Moss Ironworks, used as Christian Frederik's headquarters and the signing place of the Convention of Moss in August 1814, distinct from the full ironworks landscape.
identity.identityProblem: The record combines a large former industrial community with one surviving building of exceptional political importance. A precise canonical point can follow Konventionsgården, but it cannot represent the geometry of the whole ironworks, waterfall or later Peterson complex.
identity.splitReason: Konventionsgården is the coherent physical anchor for the combined interpretation. Workers' housing, Mossefossen and industrial remains can remain contextual or separate places.

evidence.finding: Moss Ironworks was founded in 1704 and operated from 1707 to 1876. Konventionsgården was the preserved main building where the Convention of Moss was signed in 1814.
evidence.reason: Defines the combined industrial and political identity.
